issues.t: Transmission stops engaging Drive or Reverse
issues.sym: The car suddenly acts like it is in Neutral and coasts, the engine revs without moving, shifts slip or flare, or the overdrive light flashes. Park usually still works.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in these years is the Sable's biggest weak spot. Torque converter, pump and internal shaft failures are common between about 60,000 and 160,000 miles.
issues.next: If it slips or won't engage, stop driving and get it towed to avoid more damage. Get a transmission shop diagnosis; a rebuild is the usual fix.

issues.t: Broken front coil spring can cut a tire (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from the front, the car sitting lower on one corner, or a sudden flat tire.
issues.why: Front coil springs can corrode and break. A broken end can puncture the tire, so Ford recalled these cars (recall 04V-332) to add a spring shield or replace springs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If a spring is already broken, don't drive the car until it is replaced.

issues.t: Rear coil spring breaks
issues.sym: A clunk from the back over bumps, a rear corner sitting low, or the tire rubbing.
issues.why: Rear springs rust and crack with age, often along with worn rear struts.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected; replace springs in pairs.

issues.t: Worn struts and strut mounts
issues.sym: Bouncy ride, clunking over bumps, front end noise when turning, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Struts and their upper mounts are the most-reported repair on the Sable in TrueDelta's survey. On 2008–2009 cars, front strut mounts can clunk early.
issues.next: Have the struts and mounts checked. Replacing them as complete assemblies is often simplest.

issues.t: Clunking from sway bar end links
issues.sym: A rattle or knock from the front or rear over small bumps.
issues.why: Stabilizer bar end links and bushings wear out; they are among the most common repairs on these cars.
issues.next: Have the links checked; it is a low-cost fix.

issues.t: Worn ball joints and tie rod ends
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, clunks over bumps, or tires wearing on the edges.
issues.why: Ball joints and inner and outer tie rod ends wear with mileage on these cars.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play and get an alignment after repairs.

issues.t: Misfire from a failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Check engine light (sometimes flashing), rough idle, shaking, or hesitation when accelerating.
issues.why: Ignition coils fail with age. The DOHC and 3.5L engines use one coil per cylinder; the pushrod V6 uses a coil pack.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and the coil and plugs checked. Avoid hard driving with a flashing light.

issues.t: Clicking behind the dash or temperature stuck
issues.sym: Clicking or tapping behind the dash, or air that stays hot or cold no matter the setting.
issues.why: The small motor that moves the blend door wears its plastic gears.
issues.next: Have the actuator tested and replaced.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Cranks but won't start, stalls, or sputters and loses power at speed.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump wears out; owners report replacements from about 68,000 miles on.
issues.next: Check whether you hear the pump hum at key-on and have fuel pressure tested.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: Battery light on, dim lights, dead battery or stalling.
issues.why: Alternators wear out on these cars, and rebuilt units have been unreliable for some owners.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested and buy a quality replacement.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, low coolant, or poor heat.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears. On some pushrod V6 engines the timing cover around the pump also warps.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and replace the pump before it overheats the engine.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket leak on the DOHC V6
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle, stalling at stops, or a whistle from the engine.
issues.why: The lower intake manifold gaskets on the Duratec V6 leak vacuum with age.
issues.next: Have a smoke test done to find the leak. Replace the gaskets and any cracked vacuum hoses.

issues.t: Stalling from a leaking PCV hose
issues.sym: Rough idle, stalling after refueling or at stops, or a check engine light for a lean condition.
issues.why: The PCV valve and its plastic hose crack and leak air on the Duratec V6.
issues.next: Have the PCV hose and valve inspected; they are cheap parts.

issues.t: A/C compressor or clutch fails
issues.sym: A/C blows warm, a grinding or rattling noise when the A/C is on.
issues.why: The compressor clutch and bearing or the compressor itself wear out.
issues.next: Have the system diagnosed before recharging; a failed clutch alone is cheaper than a full compressor.

issues.t: Rear drum brake wheel cylinder leaks
issues.sym: Brake fluid inside the rear wheels, a soft pedal, or grabbing rear brakes.
issues.why: The rear wheel cylinders on drum-brake versions start to leak with age.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected and replace both cylinders with new shoes if fluid has soaked them.

issues.t: Clicking when turning from a worn CV axle
issues.sym: Clicking or popping when turning sharply, or grease thrown inside the wheel from a torn boot.
issues.why: The CV joint boots tear and the joint wears once dirt gets in.
issues.next: Replace the axle once it clicks; it can eventually break.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, misfires, or the engine won't run.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner can wear out, letting the chain slap.
issues.next: Have any rattle diagnosed quickly; a jumped chain can damage the engine.

issues.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: Low coolant with no visible leak, a sweet smell, steam, overheating, or milky oil.
issues.why: The 3.5L V6 has its water pump inside the engine, driven by the timing chain. When its seal fails, coolant can leak into the oil and ruin the engine bearings.
issues.next: If coolant keeps dropping, have the oil checked for coolant right away. Do not keep driving on contaminated oil.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out
issues.sym: A pop when turning, then sudden heavy steering, or assist that comes and goes or only works in one direction.
issues.why: A failing seal inside the steering rack can overload the electro-hydraulic power steering pump, so dealers have replaced pumps before finding the rack.
issues.next: Drive carefully and have the system diagnosed at a shop that knows these cars. Ask them to check the rack before replacing the pump.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic shifts roughly or hesitates
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, a clunk into gear, or hesitation when pulling away.
issues.why: The six-speed automatic on the 3.5L can shift poorly; software updates helped some cars.
issues.next: Have the fluid checked and ask a dealer about transmission software updates first.

issues.t: Transmission cooler line leak
issues.sym: Red fluid under the front of the car, a grinding noise on shifts, or a low-fluid warning.
issues.why: Transmission cooler lines and fittings, and on some cars the cooler or seals, leak fluid.
issues.next: Check under the car for red fluid and have the lines replaced before the transmission runs low.

issues.t: A/C condenser leaks
issues.sym: The A/C slowly stops blowing cold and needs repeated recharges.
issues.why: The A/C condenser at the front of the car develops leaks.
issues.next: Have a leak test done with dye before paying for another recharge.

issues.t: Stalling or rough idle from a dirty idle air valve
issues.sym: Hard starting when cold, stalling at stops or idle, an idle that hunts up and down, or hesitation when accelerating.
issues.why: The idle air control (bypass) valve gets clogged with carbon or fails. RepairPal lists it as the most commonly reported Sable problem.
issues.next: Have the valve cleaned or replaced, and check for vacuum leaks at the same time.

issues.t: Oil pan gasket leak
issues.sym: Oil spots under the engine, a burning oil smell, or smoke when oil drips onto the exhaust.
issues.why: The oil pan gasket hardens and leaks with age.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the gasket replaced, since oil on the exhaust can be a fire risk.

issues.t: Car may roll away in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car can move as if in Neutral even though the shifter shows Park.
issues.why: Shift linkage and park pawl problems could keep Park from engaging (recalls 96V-176, 96V-166 and 96V-086). Always use the parking brake.
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Transmission fluid can leak onto the exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from under the car.
issues.why: Leaking transmission fluid could be ignited by the hot catalytic converter (recall 97V-097).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Brake warning light may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The red brake warning light stays on all the time, or never comes on.
issues.why: A faulty brake fluid level switch may not warn the driver about low brake fluid (recall 96V-016).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Brake lights may not work right (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay on or don't come on, the car won't shift out of Park, or cruise control won't engage.
issues.why: The brake light switch or its wiring can fail (recalls 01V-078 and 04V-106).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Brake and gas pedals set too close (recall)
issues.sym: Your foot can catch both pedals, especially with power-adjustable pedals moved close.
issues.why: The distance between the pedals could cause unintended acceleration or difficulty stopping (recall 02V-266).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop or run slowly.
issues.why: Water could enter the wiper motor through its cover and stop it (recall 01V-258).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Headlights may be hard to turn on (recall)
issues.sym: The headlight switch does not turn the headlights on reliably.
issues.why: A headlamp switch fault (recall 01V-075).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Air filter can smolder or burn (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: Certain air filter paper could be ignited and damage the intake or start an underhood fire (recall 04V-105).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Windshield may not be fully bonded (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: The windshield might not stay in place in a crash, reducing occupant protection (recall 03V-087).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Front airbag may not inflate properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually none. The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: The second stage of a front airbag may not inflate correctly in a crash (recall 16V-247).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.
